title: Seven Seasons and One Crack
subtitle: 饮食与器具 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与器具（历史社会与文化·饮食文化与器具）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与器具（历史社会与文化·饮食文化与器具）　|　核心词汇：cup　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cup 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my grandmother ① handed me a cup that no shop in the town would have replaced, and she said the handing was the whole of the welcome. The ② cup, meaning the drinking and not the prize, ran seven seasons and stayed unwashed on the shelf; a cup, she said, is the only thing in a kitchen that is judged by how long it is left standing.

Every ③ cup in that house had the same crack against it, and the ④ cup at the end, meaning the one she kept for the guests and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked after twice. A cup, my mother said, is nine parts welcome and one part somebody willing to pour; my grandmother said the pouring is the part that fills seven seasons.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the cup was the whole of the season, meaning the trophy and not the drinking. The ⑥ cup, meaning the trophy and not any of that, is the only thing in a season that everybody lifts and nobody keeps; cup, he said, is either something you hand or the only word that means both a drinking and a trophy. He said the trophy is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ cup had become a line in a fixture list, and the list had become an argument about the crack. The ⑧ cup of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in April, was one kitchen and seven seasons of pouring; cup, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to pour. She said the pouring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cup I remember is the one at the end, which was lifted in 1970 and is still described as the heaviest in the county. A ⑩ cup, my grandmother said in 1972, is the only thing that improves by being poured into; every cup, she said, is a trophy that has agreed to look like a drinking. She said the trophy was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 杯子（指用来喝东西的那一只）
B. n. 杯子（指喝东西这件事本身，与那个奖品相对）
C. 固定搭配：hand sb a cup 递给某人一只杯子
D. n. 杯子（指留给客人的那一只）
E. n. 杯子；杯中物（抽象总称，指一屋子的待客之道）
F. n. 奖杯（指赛程表上写到的那一个）
G. n. 奖杯（指整个赛季争夺的那一个）
H. n. 奖杯（抽象总称，指被举起的那件奖品）

items.q: handed me a cup that no shop in the town would have replaced

answers.why: hand sb a cup 意为“递给某人一只杯子”，1955 年祖母递给我一只全镇没有一家店铺肯换的杯子。
cup 意为“杯子”，指喝东西这件事本身而不是那个奖品，它在架子上搁了七个季节没洗。
cup 意为“杯子”，指那栋房子里每一只杯子，每一只都有同一道裂纹。
cup 意为“杯子”，指留给客人的那一只，是唯一有人问过第二次的。
cup 意为“奖杯”，指整个赛季争夺的那一个，父亲说这个奖杯就是那个赛季的全部。
cup 意为“奖杯”，指被举起的那件奖品而不是别的，是一个赛季里人人都举、却无人留得住的东西。
cup 意为“奖杯”，指赛程表上写到的那一个，到 1963 年这个奖杯成了赛程表里的一行。
cup 意为“杯子、杯中物”，祖母四月写道，整件事的杯子是一只杯子和七个季节的倒水待客。
cup 意为“奖杯”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1970 年被举起，至今仍被说成全县最重的。
cup 为抽象总称，祖母 1972 年说，一只杯子是唯一会因为被倒进东西而变得更好的东西。
